purpose: Define versioned, product- and domain-neutral, fail-closed documentation preparation for qualified review of potential Article 9 special-category conditions and Article 10 controls for one proposed processing activity. It records evidence-reference requirements and explicit qualified non-applicability disposition requirements only; it is not an instance schema or runtime validator and cannot determine a condition, lawfulness, or applicability; authorize processing; establish trusted scope; grant authority; decide release; or enable runtime behavior.

authoritative_external_reference.review_reference: Article 9 and Article 10; any applicability, special-category classification, condition, safeguard, criminal-offence-data disposition, or lawfulness conclusion requires qualified deployment-specific review.

documentation_preparation_boundary.non_claim: This contract does not validate an intake instance, enforce an Article 9 prohibition, authorize Article 10 processing, or satisfy the operational acceptance criteria of S1-14.4.

verified_facts: Neural Brain is product- and domain-neutral and has no accepted scoped customer or domain integration.

The current repository does not establish a concrete controller, processing activity, intended purpose, data-subject population, data category, special-category condition, Article 10 disposition, safeguard, retention period, rights process, transfer fact, or jurisdictional fact.
The repository's protected Memory Core is an internal subsystem and cannot narrow the complete cognitive-system product boundary established by ADR-018.
unknown_facts_not_inferred: whether GDPR, Article 9, or Article 10 applies to a concrete deployment or processing activity
whether personal data, special-category data, or criminal-offence data are involved
which Article 9 condition, if any, may be available or whether a condition, safeguard, minimisation, retention, rights, or transfer requirement is met
whether a concrete system may process personal data, be deployed, released, or operated

special_category_evidence_intake_templat.assessment_unit: One immutable artifact version or digest, concrete proposed deployment and processing activity, immutable authenticated Tenant, Area, and Project scope references, intended-purpose contract version, activity/purpose reference combination, and jurisdiction evidence.

evidence_or_qualified_not_applicable_sem.selection_rule: For every potentially applicable Article 9 condition and the Article 10 control, record exactly one of scope-matched candidate evidence or a qualified not-applicable disposition.
evidence_or_qualified_not_applicable_sem.placeholder_rule: Blank, TODO, TBD, pending, unknown-as-not-applicable, illustrative, unresolved, or non-resolving references are placeholders and satisfy neither branch.
evidence_or_qualified_not_applicable_sem.both_or_neither_rule: Both branches populated, neither branch populated, or any placeholder reference makes the documentation preparation incomplete and keeps deployment-specific release blocked.

scope_binding_requirements: Tenant, Area, and Project references must identify immutable authenticated runtime-scope evidence. An intake identifier, purpose label, activity label, request payload, prompt, observation, model response, memory content, or tool output cannot establish, broaden, or substitute trusted scope.

Purpose and activity references must name immutable versioned evidence. A special-category evidence intake is valid only for its exact artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, and jurisdiction combination; evidence may not be reused across Tenant, Area, Project, purpose, activity, artifact, jurisdiction, data category, recipient, or transfer changes without a separate record and qualified review.

The intake must contain durable evidence references and categories only. It must not contain raw personal data, special-category values, criminal-offence data, personal identifiers, credentials, secrets, prompts, memory payloads, consent text, contracts, legal advice, or unverified external assertions.

Article 9 condition candidates, Article 10 dispositions, safeguards, minimisation, retention, rights, transfer, external facts, and non-applicability assertions must identify their source, provenance, date, currency, scope, reviewer treatment, and contradiction status. Unknown, stale, contradictory, unauthenticated, or unqualified facts remain explicit release blockers rather than inferred favorable facts.
deterministic_review_order: Verify every required field, exact immutable artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, jurisdiction, accountable owner, qualified reviewer, review date, evidence reference, and reassessment trigger; any absent, unknown, stale, contradictory, non-immutable, or scope-mismatched fact is incomplete.

Verify linked RoPA, GDPR role, GDPR applicability, Article 6, use-case, and reassessment evidence for the same artifact, authenticated scope, purpose, activity, and jurisdiction; a missing or conflicting prerequisite remains a release blocker.

Apply the exactly-one candidate-evidence-or-qualified-not-applicable rule separately to every potentially applicable Article 9 condition, without classifying data, selecting, validating, or concluding a condition. Reject placeholders, both branches, or neither branch.

Apply the same rule to Article 10. Candidate evidence must address processing under official authority or authorization by Union or Member State law, appropriate safeguards, and whether any comprehensive register is controlled under official authority; a qualified not-applicable disposition must be scope-matched and evidence-backed. Missing, unknown, disputed, placeholder, or scope-mismatched evidence remains a release blocker and cannot be inferred as non-applicable.

Record safeguards, necessity, data minimisation, retention, deletion, data-subject rights, recipients, processors, locations, transfers, and external facts as qualified-review evidence only; no favorable later fact compensates for an unresolved earlier fact.

Record explicit non-applicability, unknown, conflict, evidence-expiry, gap, and blocker dispositions with provenance and reviewer treatment, reassessment triggers, next review date, and the independent release-decision reference. A completed intake remains evidence input only and cannot create a legal, authority, processing, deployment, release, or runtime outcome.

authority_boundary.template_is: versioned documentation preparation for a separately governed qualified legal/privacy review
template_is_not: a legal opinion, Article 9 condition determination, Article 10 determination, or compliance certification

a determination of lawfulness, special-category classification, condition validity, safeguard sufficiency, minimisation, retention, deletion, data-subject rights, transfer validity, or a GDPR exemption
an authenticated Tenant, Area, Project, Session, principal, role, authority, policy, or approval context
a policy decision, Security Floor override, protected-state transition request, or gate decision
a processing, deployment, productive-use, or release approval
a runtime capability enablement or external-effect authorization
an instance schema, executable validator, Article 9 enforcement mechanism, Article 10 register, or official-authority control
an implementation, maturity, recognition, safety, product capability, or production-autonomy claim
authority_boundary.release_boundary: Only separately applicable qualified review, accepted governance, and all Protected Control Plane, transition-gate, evaluation, recognition, and release evidence requirements may decide a concrete processing activity or deployment. This intake never activates a runtime path.

current_blocker.unblock_condition: A concrete proposed deployment supplies every required field, exact immutable artifact and authenticated scope/purpose/activity/jurisdiction evidence, linked prerequisite evidence, qualified reviewer and external-fact provenance, deterministic candidate evidence or qualified not-applicable dispositions for every Article 9 condition and Article 10 control, Article 10 official-authority or Union/Member-State-law authorization and safeguards evidence where applicable, comprehensive-register control evidence where applicable, minimisation/retention/rights/transfer evidence, an accepted typed instance-validation contract and operational enforcement where required, reassessment triggers, and separately governed release evidence.
current_blocker.next_step: Create one immutable Article 9 special-category evidence intake per proposed artifact, authenticated Tenant/Area/Project scope, purpose, processing activity, and jurisdiction before any processing-specific or deployment-specific release decision.
